description.content:
get a list of columns

**Required Role:** Viewer or higher

query.description: A comma separated list of select star data_types to filter for columns that are of those dataTypes.
A comma separated list of database guids to filter for items within those databases.
A comma separated list of data source guids to filter for items within those data sources.
A comma separated list of tag guids
A list of dbt project guids to filter these columns for. The returned values will be dbt models
Calculate and include total object counts in the response.
Filters by is_join_key field value.
A boolean which filters for newest tables in the organization.
A flag that filters out any tables with descriptions
A flag that shows only tables with no downstream lineage
A flag that filters out any table that has a popularity rating.
A flag that filters out any tagged tables
A flag that shows only tables with no upstream lineage

Specify the ordering for the results. 

 A comma separated list for ordering by multiple fields and a preceding `-` indicates reverse order. 

Note: Order is case-sensitive.
A page number within the paginated result set.
Number of results to return per page.
A comma separated list of popularity ranges (inclusive) can include integers from 1-100 ex) 1-10,90-100 would be the bottom 10 percent and the top 10 percent, respectively. Ranges can overlap.
A comma separated list of schema guids to filter for columns within those schemas
Search a column with multiple types of params in one go
Search for an asset using its description
Search for columns given an external type
Search for columns given a data type
Search for columns given a formula
Search for columns given a label
Search for columns given a column name (goes upto data source name)
Search for an asset using a tag name
A comma separated list of tag guids
A comma separated list of table guids to filter for columns within those tables

Filter objects by updated_on. May specify __gt, __gte, __lt or __lte.

 API call to: 

 ENDPOINT/updated_on__gt=2021-08-04T15:12:40&updated_on__lt=2021-08-23 

 will result with objects updated_on after  August 4th 2021 at 15:12:40, but before August 23rd 2021. 

. If you want to include lower or upper bound of the range use __gte or __lte respectively.
